- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average if no strong event context.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent auction supply; dampen forecast growth by 0.5–1.0% per event beyond 15.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility; use weighted average of 3-day and 7-day moving averages for smoothing.
